theThreeDefinitions_reconciled.whichInstrumentTheCeilingMustDeriveFrom: TESTED THE INTEGRATION SEAT'S HYPOTHESIS ('the ceiling is derived from the staged table by the rail's own query; the live probe audits staging currency') AND FOUND IT WRONG, WITH EVIDENCE: hauska-engine's tx_zoning_district_staging has no live production consumer for Elgin. Its only two consumers are (a) join-zoning-district-to-parcels.mjs, whose own docstring states it is 'ONLY ever run here against Lockhart; running it for any other city is a separate, explicit decision' (grepped: it has no other invocation anywhere in the repo, no CI/cloudbuild wiring, only its own package.json script entry), and (b) drain.ts's drainZoningStagingRows(), whose own header states it is a 'READ-ONLY shape for a FUTURE Factory 2 zoning writer... Does NOT mint atoms, does NOT stamp parcels' (grepped: its only callers are drain-tx-zoning-district-staging.mjs, a standalone manual script, and unit tests). Elgin's staged data has therefore never been drained into atoms, txgio_parcel.zoning_district, or anything parcel_record_cell could read. Instrument B (the staged-table join, 48/58/525) is structurally disconnected from the rail today. Instrument A (the live probe, 9/457) is the one that actually measured against txgio_parcel.zoning_district -- the column the 2026-09-08 close's own finding says the rail's re-bake needs to read from ('hauska-factory needs to re-bake parcel_record_cell's zoningDistrict rail from the now-current txgio_parcel state'). The integration seat's clean two-instruments-two-jobs framing describes a plausible FUTURE architecture (once a real Factory-2 zoning writer exists to drain tx_zoning_district_staging into atoms) but not the current one.

trueceiling_reportedNotWritten.derivation: The ceiling bounds the rail's own unaccounted-cell residue, so it must be measured over the SAME population the rail measures (its own narrowed unaccounted-cell set, not the full in-city population) and via the SAME data path the rail actually reads today (txgio_parcel.zoning_district, populated by legacy-design-tools' stamp mechanism -- confirmed the only live path, since hauska-engine's staged-table pipeline for Elgin is unconsumed, per theThreeDefinitions_reconciled above). Instrument A (the live probe) is the only one of the three that measured against that population and that path. Instrument B's 48/58/525 describes a real, useful, but currently-disconnected pipeline stage -- informative for a future Factory-2 writer, not a valid ceiling input today. The ceiling was therefore not wrong to be 9/457; per the retiring planner's own note quoted in the dispatch, it was wrong to be COMPARED against a live 'measured residue' whose provenance nobody confirmed matches its population -- and this lane's evidence says instrument A, not instrument B, is the one that actually does.
trueceiling_reportedNotWritten.residualUncertainty: This lane cannot confirm what population/predicate factory-parcel-r5-zoning's live query itself uses (hauska-factory, out of scope) -- only that it is NOT reading hauska-engine's staged table for Elgin, because nothing currently drains that table into anything rail-visible. If the gate's 'measured residue exceeds ceiling' refusal is actually driven by a live computation over the staged table (contradicting everything found here), that would mean some OTHER, unfound consumer exists -- this lane searched hauska-engine exhaustively (grep for every reference to tx_zoning_district_staging and drainZoningStagingRows) and found none, but a hauska-factory-side consumer calling the same table directly (cross-repo, cross-database) cannot be ruled out from here. Recommend the integration seat confirm factory-parcel-r5-zoning's actual data source as the one remaining decisive check.

The live Elgin_Zoning FeatureServer/0 (Bastrop side) carries 11 features with Zone_Code='S-P' as of 2026-09-09, unmapped by this repo's codeDomainMap; 9 of those 11 polygons geometrically cover 10 named Bastrop residue prop_ids (12948, 111348, 14457, 124619, 12830, 8712013, 60891, 11364, 85259, 14535).

'The layer is the same, only staleness differs' is not a safe assumption for a live public ArcGIS layer even over one month -- Elgin's live layer 0 gained (or always had, differently-coded) an 11-feature 'S-P' (Specific Use) district class between whatever vintage the registry's codeDomainMap was authored against and today, and a codeDomainMap with an explicit allow-list (rather than a deny-list or pass-through default) will silently and correctly-per-its-own-contract drop real, live district coverage for any code it doesn't yet know about. Anyone re-staging a codeDomainMap-gated city layer should diff the live layer's own distinct code values against the map's keys, not just re-run the fetch.

A staging table with a write path (stage-tx-zoning-district.mjs) but only a single-city-piloted, explicitly-scoped consumer (join-zoning-district-to-parcels.mjs, 'ONLY ever run here against Lockhart') and an explicitly-labeled future-only drain interface (drain.ts: 'READ-ONLY shape for a FUTURE Factory 2 zoning writer') is a real, live-written table that is nonetheless NOT part of any current production data path for any other city. Before trusting a hypothesis like 'X feeds the rail,' grep for X's actual callers -- a table can be genuinely, verifiably live and simultaneously disconnected from everything downstream.

The decisive remaining check is factory-parcel-r5-zoning's own live query in hauska-factory: what population and predicate does it actually use to compute the 'measured Elgin residue' the dispatch says exceeds 9/457? This lane's evidence strongly implies it is NOT reading hauska-engine's tx_zoning_district_staging for Elgin (nothing drains that table to anything rail-visible), but could not open hauska-factory to confirm directly, per this dispatch's explicit hauska-engine-only scope. Whoever owns that repo should confirm; if confirmed, 9/457 is the correct ceiling as-is and the original guard refusal is a genuine, real, and currently still-open GIS-gap block on Bastrop/Travis launch, not a units mismatch to fix in code.

Unresolved secondary question: does legacy-design-tools' own zoning-layers.ts registry (the one that produced the 9/457 probe) have the same S-P code-domain gap this lane found in hauska-engine's registry.ts? If so, some of the 9 (48021) / 457 (48453) 'confirmed real GIS gap' parcels may themselves be S-P-covered-but-unmapped rather than genuinely uncovered, meaning even 9/457 could shrink further with a codeDomainMap fix rather than requiring an operator ruling of 'refused'. Out of this lane's scope (different repo) to check.

Whether to add an 'S-P' entry to hauska-engine's elgin-tx codeDomainMap (registry.ts) is a real, narrowly-scoped, evidence-backed fix this lane identified but did not apply, being outside a 're-stage-and-reconcile' mandate. Recommend a short, separate, explicitly-scoped follow-on lane for it if the operator wants Elgin's Specific-Use districts recognized -- it would move 10 parcels from 'unmatched' to 'matched' in hauska-engine's own staged-table measurement (58 -> 48 again, but now because the true cause is understood, not by coincidence).

This lane's own restage moved Bastrop's staged-table residue (48 -> 58) even though nothing currently reads that table for Elgin -- meaning this lane's live write, while correctly scoped and verified, has NO effect on anything gate-visible today. If the integration seat wants hauska-engine's staged Elgin data to actually matter for the launch gate, wiring a Factory-2-style drain/apply path (per drain.ts's own stated intent) for elgin-tx and elgin-tx-travis, the way join-zoning-district-to-parcels.mjs already does for Lockhart, is the missing link -- not measured or attempted here, named because this lane surfaced exactly why it's missing.
